About the role
Melbourne Automotive Engineering has been delivering trusted repairs, diagnostics, and tuning from our Bundoora workshop to Melbourne drivers and major insurers alike. With a scope that covers everything from routine servicing through to complete engine rebuilds, we are now looking for an experienced Mechanic to join our team. This is a hands-on trade role for someone who takes their work seriously and holds themselves to a high standard on every job, regardless of what comes through the door.

Key responsibilities
- Work across a steady mix of servicing and repair jobs, managing your own time and keeping jobs moving without sacrificing the standard of work
- Diagnose problems properly, using both hands-on knowledge and electronic diagnostic equipment to find the actual fault before touching anything
- Carry out repairs and mechanical rebuilds accurately, using manufacturer documentation as the benchmark and verifying your work before anything goes back to the customer
- Handle routine maintenance with the same attention as the bigger jobs, because preventative work done well keeps customers off the lift longer
- Assess vehicles for roadworthiness and prepare accurate reports or certificates where your qualifications allow

About you
- Trade-qualified mechanic (or with relevant experience) with genuine workshop experience and the diagnostic ability to back it up
- Someone who takes pride in their work and doesn't cut corners when rebuilding or reassembling
- Comfortable with computerised diagnostic tools and able to interpret what they're telling you
- Organised and self-directed, able to move between jobs without losing focus on quality
- Current driver's licence essential

A leadership opportunity in the heart of the Riverina.

Leeton Health Service is an integral rural facility within Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), delivering essential inpatient, outpatient and community-focused care to Leeton and surrounding communities. Enjoy Leeton's vibrant regional lifestyle, known for its rich agricultural heritage, Art Deco charm, local caf s and strong community spirit - with easy access to Griffith (30 mins), Wagga Wagga (1.5 hrs), Canberra (2.5 hrs) and Melbourne (5 hrs).

As the Facility Manager you will be responsible for the day-to-day operational management of nursing and other clinical and non-clinical support services at the facility level. The role ensures the delivery of safe, compassionate and person-centred care, through the assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care in collaboration with individuals and the multidisciplinary health care team, to achieve safe, high-quality care outcomes that meet the goals of each person at the facility.

To find out more, please review the Position Description

Our ideal candidate will:

Hold current authority to practise as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA, with demonstrated capability consistent with Appendix 1 (Core knowledge and skills of Nurse Manager Grade 3) of the Public Health System Nurses' and Midwives' (State) Award 2015.

Demonstrate proven senior leadership and operational management experience, supported by qualifications in health management, health policy and planning, business or equivalent, or currently working towards relevant postgraduate qualifications.

Demonstrate exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to liaise, negotiate and influence effectively with clinicians, managers, staff, and key stakeholders, including demonstrated capability in conflict resolution.

Demonstrate high-level computer literacy, including experience with health-related systems and a range of workforce and performance-analytics platforms.

Provide evidence of successful achievement in financial and activity-service delivery management, including the ability to identify efficiencies, develop strategies and meet organisational performance targets.

Demonstrate strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, inspire and manage teams, applying recognised change management principles to achieve service and organisational goals.

Demonstrate sound understanding of, and experience with, accreditation requirements and the link between accreditation, clinical governance, and quality and safety improvement.

Demonstrate experience managing a complex clinical service with competing demands relating to access, patient flow-throughput, workforce capability, and resource allocation.

Hold a current Class C Driver Licence and demonstrate the ability and willingness to travel as required across MLHD, including driving long distances when necessary.
 

Why join MLHD:

At Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), we offer more than a job - we offer the chance to make a real difference.

Full-Time: Immediate start
Job Title: Welder
Salary range: $79,500 - $86,600 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role
Our client is a leading steel fabricator specializing in large-scale structural projects bridges, mining infrastructure, and commercial buildings. Precision, quality, and safety are at the core of their workshop operations. We are recruiting an experienced Welder to join their team and deliver high-integrity welds on heavy steel sections to exact engineering specifications.

Key Duties and Responsibilities
• Interpret detailed engineering drawings, blueprints, and welding specification sheets to determine material grades, joint configurations, and correct welding procedures.
• Select, inspect, and prepare metal stock; cut marked-out structural sections using oxy-fuel torches, plasma cutters, and guillotines to precise dimensions.
• Shape and bend steel beams, channels, and pipes using hydraulic presses, bending rolls, and manual heating/hammering techniques to achieve required profiles.
• Align and fit components using clamps, jigs, and measuring tools; join sections via MIG, TIG, flux-cored arc welding, and bolting/riveting methods.
• Examine completed welds for bead width, penetration depth, and dimensional accuracy; perform visual checks and assist with non-destructive testing.
• Finish products by grinding, filing, polishing, and cleaning weld zones; apply protective coatings or acid baths as per project standards.

Requirements
• Minimum two years’ welding experience in structural steel fabrication; relevant trade certificate (or equivalent) and current welding certifications.
• Strong ability to read and interpret technical drawings and welding symbols; thorough knowledge of weld procedures and site safety protocols.
• Capable of welding in all positions on heavy plate and sections; comfortable operating overhead cranes and workshop machinery.
• Relevant qualification to above field.

Apply now 
Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter detailing your relevant experience in Welder. Applications will be reviewed as received, therefore, please apply as soon as possible before the closing date.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Placed.au is looking for a full-time Baker for our client in Lavington, New South Wales. This role is responsible for preparing, baking, and finishing baked goods such as bread, rolls, pastries, and other baked products while ensuring quality, consistency, and adherence to food safety standards.

Job Description

Product

•	Weighing up and mixing as per recipe requirements.

•	Hand shaping and molding as instructed by Bakery Manager.

•	Maintaining quality and consistency standards.

•	Producing bread quantities in an efficient and timely manner to meet production forecast set by Bakery Manager.

Operations

•	Compliance with all workplace OH&S Laws.

•	Compliance with all Food Safety Standards.

•	Maintain the highest standards of cleanliness.

•	Report required equipment and kitchen maintenance.

•	Complete all daily, weekly and monthly FSP tasks as required.

Leadership

•	Maintaining a positive work culture and a 'Can Do' attitude.

•	Supporting fellow team members to achieve common goals.

•	Supervise Apprentice and Baker's Assistant as well as providing training to them.

•	Participate in baking workshops, forums and competitions when required.

Qualifications / Attributes

•	Must hold a Certificate III in Baking including at least two (2) years of on-the-job training, or at least three (3) years of relevant work experience may substitute for the formal qualification.

•	Must possess at least one (1) year of relevant work experience as a Baker or in a similar commercial bakery role.

•	Demonstrated ability to produce baked goods to consistent quality and weight standards.

•	Strong knowledge of food safety standards and OH&S requirements in a bakery environment.

•	Ability to work efficiently and meet daily production targets within rostered hours.

•	Strong teamwork and communication skills with the ability to support and lead junior staff.

Salary

$75,000 – $85,000 per annum excluding superannuation.
